title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Relevant Persons
tiers.description: All Directors and other Company officers, Executives and Employees of the Company and their related parties, and may include contractors, consultants and advisers from time to time. Subject to the General Prohibition, short-term trading restriction, margin lending/encumbrance restriction and hedging restriction.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: The Company's Directors, Executives, and Band A, B, C and D Employees (as defined by the Company's Remuneration Framework) and their related parties. Subject to the quarterly Blackout Periods (Closed Periods) in addition to the rules applying to Relevant Persons generally.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: AIC Mines Directors; subject to an additional standing requirement to notify the whole Board of an intention to trade (including in financial products over the Company's securities) at all times, whether or not an Open Period applies, and to notify the Company Secretary of completed trades within 3 business days for ASX Listing Rule 3.19A purposes.

definitions.hedging_definition: hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of put and call options or other derivative instruments)

windows.end_anchor: release of the December quarterly report, plus 24 hours
release of the March quarterly report, plus 24 hours
release of the June quarterly report, plus 24 hours
release of the September quarterly report, plus 24 hours

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may notify a Relevant Person that they may not trade during all or part of an Open Period where the Company is in possession of inside information. The Chairman may direct that the standard quarterly Blackout Periods not apply. Confidentiality of either action is not addressed.

rules.section: Trading in the Company's Securities, Derivative Products and Margin Lending Arrangements
rules.detail: Financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities (i.e. derivatives, with no venue limitation) are expressly swept into the same 'trading' concept as ordinary share dealing; there is no outright ban, but all the usual rules (blackout periods, Director notification, general inside-information prohibition, hedging rule for unvested plan securities) apply to them.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are prohibited from trading in the Company's securities or in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities, in accordance with this policy.

rules.section: Guidelines for Dealing in Securities - Directors
rules.detail: Directors must notify the whole Board of an intention to trade in financial products created over the Company's securities before doing so, at all times, irrespective of whether an Open Period applies.
rules.evidence: At all times prior to trading in the Company's securities or in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities (whether or not an Open Period applies), Directors must notify the whole Board of Directors of their intention to trade and confirm that they are not in possession of any inside information.

rules.detail: During the four quarterly Blackout Periods (and for 24 hours after they end), Designated Persons may not trade in financial products created over the Company's securities, unless the Chairman directs otherwise or Exceptional Circumstances clearance is obtained.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons (including Directors for which additional notification requirements are applicable – see above) may NOT trade in the Company's securities on the ASX or financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities during, nor for twenty four (24) hours following the end of, the following Blackout Periods.

rules.section: Trading in the Company's Securities, Derivative Products and Margin Lending Arrangements
rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging (including put and call options) over unvested securities issued under an employee or Director option or share plan.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons must not engage in hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of put and call options or other derivative instruments) over unvested Securities issued pursuant to any employee or Director option or share plan.

rules.section: Trading in the Company's Securities, Derivative Products and Margin Lending Arrangements
rules.detail: Hedging over vested securities is expressly contemplated and not banned, but must comply with the rest of the policy (blackout periods, Director notification, general inside-information prohibition); no dedicated approval process is named for hedging itself.
rules.evidence: In addition, any hedging over vested Securities must comply with this policy.

rules.section: Trading in the Company's Securities, Derivative Products and Margin Lending Arrangements
rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure is a financial product created in respect of the Company's securities, so it is treated as 'trading' subject to the general framework, and any secured element would separately require prior written Board approval under the margin lending/encumbrance rule.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are prohibited from trading in the Company's securities or in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities, in accordance with this policy.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named; only short-term/speculative trading is separately addressed, which is a different concept.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

rules.section: Trading in the Company's Securities, Derivative Products and Margin Lending Arrangements
rules.detail: CFDs are not named but are a financial product created in respect of the Company's securities, so are treated as 'trading' subject to the general framework rather than being separately banned.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are prohibited from trading in the Company's securities or in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities, in accordance with this policy.

rules.section: Trading in the Company's Securities, Derivative Products and Margin Lending Arrangements
rules.detail: Margin lending arrangements where the lender is given rights over the Relevant Person's interest in the securities are prohibited unless prior written Board approval is obtained; there is no absolute ban.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into Margin Lending arrangements, whereby lenders are provided with rights over their interests in the Company's securities, without prior written Board approval.

rules.section: Trading in the Company's Securities, Derivative Products and Margin Lending Arrangements
rules.detail: The margin lending clause is drafted broadly around lenders being 'provided with rights over their interests' in the securities, which functionally covers any encumbrance, not just formally-labelled margin loans; prior written Board approval removes the prohibition.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into Margin Lending arrangements, whereby lenders are provided with rights over their interests in the Company's securities, without prior written Board approval.

rules.section: Trading in the Company's Securities, Derivative Products and Margin Lending Arrangements
rules.detail: Any secured financing arrangement giving the financier rights over the individual's interest in the securities (not limited to margin loans in the narrow sense) requires prior written Board approval; no periodic disclosure obligation is stated.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into Margin Lending arrangements, whereby lenders are provided with rights over their interests in the Company's securities, without prior written Board approval.

rules.detail: Expressed as an expectation ('should not') rather than an absolute bar, with no defined holding period, no stated basis, and no clearance mechanism referenced.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons should not engage in short-term or speculative trading of the Company's securities.

clearance.section: Guidelines for Dealing in Securities - Directors; Notification of Trade in Company Securities
clearance.evidence: Directors must notify the whole Board of Directors of their intention to trade and confirm that they are not in possession of any inside information. ... Directors must also notify the Company Secretary of any trade in the Company's securities within three (3) business days of such trade occurring

clearance.section: Trades excluded from the Share Trading Policy
clearance.evidence: The requirement to provide notice of an intention to trade in the Company's securities does not apply to the acquisition of securities through: ... However, the requirement does apply to the trading of those securities once they have been acquired.

short_term.evidence: Relevant Persons should not engage in short-term or speculative trading of the Company's securities.

exceptions.approver: Chairman (or, if unavailable, the Chief Executive Officer and Company Secretary)
exceptions.evidence: Clearance to trade in the Company's securities inside of the defined Closed Periods may be granted in exceptional circumstances at the discretion of the Chairman (or if unavailable, the Chief Executive Officer and Company Secretary). Exceptional circumstances would include, but not be limited to cases of severe financial hardship

exceptions.approver: Chairman (or, if unavailable, the Chief Executive Officer and Company Secretary)
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances would include, but not be limited to cases of severe financial hardship, where court orders exist or other overriding legal or statutory circumstance requiring the sale or transfer of the securities.
The requirement to provide notice of an intention to trade in the Company's securities does not apply to the acquisition of securities through: A Company Employee Incentive Plan or Scheme
The Share Trading Policy does not apply where there is no change in beneficial interest in the securities.
The Share Trading Policy does not apply to the disposal of securities by acceptance of takeover offers.

exemption_authority: The Chairman (or, if unavailable, the CEO and Company Secretary) has discretion to grant Exceptional Circumstances clearance to trade during a Closed Period, and may direct that a standard Blackout Period not apply. The Board has authority to approve margin lending or other secured financing arrangements over a Relevant Person's securities in writing, in advance, removing the default prohibition. There is no exemption authority for the hedging ban over unvested plan securities.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending / secured financing subject to Board approval
bespoke_clauses.clause: Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into Margin Lending arrangements, whereby lenders are provided with rights over their interests in the Company's securities, without prior written Board approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike an outright ban, this policy permits a loan secured on the collared shares (or any arrangement giving the bank rights over the shares) if the Board gives prior written approval, making the financing leg of a funded collar structurally available subject to Board sign-off.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested plan securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Relevant Persons must not engage in hedging arrangements ... over unvested Securities issued pursuant to any employee or Director option or share plan. In addition, any hedging over vested Securities must comply with this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because a collar would be written over already-vested shares, the absolute hedging ban does not apply; hedging of vested shares is only subject to the general framework (blackout periods, Director notification, no inside information), not a substantive bar or a dedicated approval step.

bespoke_clauses.topic: financial products swept into blackout ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons ... may NOT trade in the Company's securities on the ASX or financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities during, nor for twenty four (24) hours following the end of, the following Blackout Periods.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The four quarterly Blackout Periods (plus a 24-hour buffer) expressly extend to derivative trades, so entry, unwind or settlement of the collar must fall within Open Periods unless the Chairman directs otherwise or Exceptional Circumstances clearance is obtained.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Unless specified otherwise, clearance to trade outside a trading window will apply for a period of ten (10) business days from the communication to the Relevant Person of the clearance to trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a Closed Period exception is needed to execute or unwind the collar, documentation must complete within a 10-business-day window from grant of clearance, a tight timetable for a bank transaction.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Notice lodged with the ASX must provide the following information: whether the trading occurred outside a Trading Window, when prior written clearance was required; whether clearance was provided to allow the Trade to proceed; and on what date clearance was provided if granted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director's entry into or unwind of a collar becomes a public ASX disclosure that flags whether it occurred outside the trading window and whether clearance was needed and granted, which the bank and director should factor into transaction timing and market messaging.

summary: A funded equity collar over vested shares appears possible for a Director or executive of AIC Mines, subject to conditions. The hedging ban in the policy applies only to unvested plan securities, so hedging (expressly including put and call options) over vested shares is permitted subject to the general framework rather than being separately prohibited. The loan leg, structured as a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement giving the bank rights over the pledged shares, is not banned outright but requires prior written Board approval before it may be entered into. Both legs, being 'financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities', are swept into the ordinary trading rules: Directors must notify the whole Board of an intention to trade at any time, execution must avoid the four quarterly Blackout Periods (plus a 24-hour buffer) unless the Chairman grants an exception or Exceptional Circumstances clearance (valid for 10 business days) is obtained, and the person must not be in possession of inside information. Because Board approval is a discretionary, case-by-case gate for the secured financing leg, the practical availability of the collar depends on obtaining that approval in addition to complying with the timing and notification rules.
